title: The Heart Sutra, alone
hookLine: read the Heart Sutra without commentary
tomorrow: why does a sutra about cutting through everything open with lunch?
last: THE SAME BOOK, A NEW READER.

lines: A LINE HERE, A GLOSS THERE.
cards: Some songs come wrapped in so much talk, the explainer video, the comments, the friend who says wait for this part, that the first clean listen never happens.
The Heart Sutra has lived like that on this path: a line here, a mantra there, a teacher's gloss on every phrase.
So today, a new block of rereading begins with the Mahayana sources, and the first one comes with nobody talking over it.

teach.b: Read alone, the shape is plain. Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, practicing deep wisdom, looks and sees that the five heaps that make a person are empty, and with that, passes beyond suffering.
Then he speaks to the monk Shariputra: form is emptiness, emptiness is form.
After that comes a long run of no: no eye, no ear, no nose, no suffering, no path, no attaining.

And then, without a pause, the sutra says the bodhisattva therefore has no fear. It ends in a mantra: gate gate paragate parasamgate bodhi svaha. With no one explaining, the strangest part is that run of no.
It doesn't sound like a sermon. It sounds like someone setting things down.

So ask the question before anyone answers it for you: what is empty? On this path, teachers have said empty doesn't mean nothing; it means nothing stands on its own. Hold that loosely today, and let the sutra speak first.

how: The Heart Sutra is chanted in Mahayana temples and Zen halls in East Asia and the West, in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Tibetan and English, often from memory.

games.q: the week's lines — tap the pairs.

s: the Heart Sutra says nothing exists at all
it says the five heaps are empty; teachers on this path read empty as not standing on its own, not as nothing.
in the Heart Sutra, Avalokiteshvara speaks to Shariputra
form is emptiness, emptiness is form is said to the monk Shariputra.
the sutra ends with a mantra
gate gate paragate parasamgate bodhi svaha.

games.q: a friend reads 'no eye, no ear, no nose' in the Heart Sutra and says Buddhists must think bodies aren't real. your best reply?
o: it says nothing stands on its own, not that nothing is there.
she's right: the sutra teaches the body is only an illusion.
it's poetry; those lines don't really mean anything at all.
games.why: the run of no follows 'form is emptiness, emptiness is form'. form is still form; it just doesn't stand alone.

practice: Listen for one sound around you, the fridge, a car, a bird, your own breath. Follow it from where it starts to where it fades, and notice what it depends on: air, distance, an ear.
When it's gone, wait for the next one, until the bell.

wordCard.voice: The Heart Sutra: a short Mahayana text in which Avalokiteshvara sees that the five heaps are empty. Today, read with no commentary at all.

orig.note: Sanskrit: emptiness; in the Heart Sutra, the five heaps are seen as empty.

carryVoice: The line to take with you: what is empty, asked before it's answered. Week's end, and a new block begun.
